title: Long Term Safety of Preoperative Percutaneous Intercostal Cryoneurolysis
official: Long Term Safety of Preoperative Percutaneous Intercostal Cryoneurolysis: Neuropathic Pain, Quality of Life and Sensory Recovery in a Paediatric Cohort Following Pectus Excavatum Repair
summary: Follow up of patients who underwent percutaneous cryoneurolysis for pectus excavatum repair (the Nuss procedure) pain management

interventions.name: Self-report Leeds Assessment of Neuropathic Symptoms and Signs (LANSS) Questionnaire - Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL™) Questionnaire - Patient Self-Assessment Sensory Scale

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients who underwent percutaneous cryoneurolysis.
* Patients who underwent surgical correction of pectus excavatum according to the Nuss procedure.
* Signed informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Refusal to participate in the study
* Peripheral nervous system disorders
* Age \< 14 years
* Failure to attend scheduled follow-up visits
